**m4-danger-paths gate went dark: environment, not code (#850)**

**What**: m4-danger-paths (upgrade/rollback/clobber/downgrade safety) stopped completing on 2026-09-03 after 22:10 UTC — cancelled at timeout-minutes: 20, on main AND on PR #849. Filed as #850.

**Why it looked like my fault**: #847 (S7) was the ONLY commit merged between the last green run (16:22) and the first cancellation (22:10). Correlation pointed straight at it.

**The control that cleared it**: re-ran the exact run that succeeded in 2 minutes at 16:20 (`gh run rerun 33778002102`) — same commit, same workflow. It also timed out at 20 minutes. Same tree, 10x slower ⇒ the tree is not the variable. Environment (runner / docker / npm in container), not brain's code.

**Learned — the method, not the fact**: when correlation names your own recent change, the cheap decisive experiment is to re-run an OLD green run of the SAME commit. It separates "my code did it" from "the world changed" in one step, and it cost one command. Without it I would have spent the session hunting a bug that does not exist in #847.

**Release impact**: the gate is not `required` at any tier so it blocks no merge, but it proves exactly the property a release cut needs (consumers run brain:upgrade). Recommendation given: merge #849, hold the publish.yml dispatch until the evidence exists — either the runner recovers or `npm run test:danger-paths` is run locally with docker.
